newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland stadium COPs to hit street May 21.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland stadium COPs to hit street May 21.

text.p: Cleveland Finance Director Martin Carmody said Wednesday the city expects to sell $130 million of certificates of participation (COPs) May 21 to help finance a new stadium for its future National Football League expansion franchise.
The new stadium will house the new Cleveland Browns on the site where the former Browns team played before the franchise relocated to Baltimore in 1995 and renamed itself the Ravens.
Cleveland has completed a preliminary offering circular for the sale, which is now being printed, Carmody said.

The NFL is expected to contribute about $48 million toward the estimated $242.8 million cost of the open-air stadium as part of an agreement permitting the franchise relocation. Cleveland met seat sales requirements for that agreement in January.
The COPs are to be paid off with revenues from taxes on parking, admissions and car rentals. A.G. Edwards & Sons has been selected to lead the syndicate for the offering.

Cleveland sold $15 million of bond anticipation notes in October to fund demolition of Municipal Stadium. Those notes may be rolled over during the construction phase and then taken out when the new stadium opens, Carmody said during an earlier interview.
